INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  Library Board
  MINUTES – September 23, 2020

The Inglewood Library Board met on September 23, 2020 on Zoom. The meeting was called to order at
6:47 p.m. by Board Member Julie Minton.

Roll Call

Present:
  Julie Minton – District 1 Board Member, Vice Chairman
  Pat Douglas – District 2 Board Member
  Ernesto Castillo – District 3 Board Member
  Jacqueline Cochran – District 4 Board Member

Absent Board Members:
  Patt Sanders – At Large Board Member, Chairman

Staff:
  Harjinder Singh – Deputy to the City Manager
  Linda Silba – Principal Librarian over Adult Services
  Kerri Arroyo – Principal Librarian at the Branch Library
  Irina Martirosian – Staff Assistant

Absent Staff:
  Frances Tracht – Library Manager

Public Comments

  None

Friends Report

  Susan Carleo, President of the Friends of Inglewood Public Library (FOIPL) told the board that
Friends of Inglewood Public Library had meetings with Mr. Singh about a lot of updates, had a walk thru the
library and saw all the changes of the library. Mrs. Carleo thanked Mr. Singh for including friends in those
meetings to hear about all the great changes of the library. Two members of FOIPL got tested and start
working with library staff, sorting the donations library received throughout the time that library has been
closed. Mrs. Carleo also thanked library employees for helping them with the donations. Next book sale
won’t be until late spring or early summer of next year.

Library Report

  Deputy to the City Manager Harjinder Singh gave an update on the Library operations.
  1
     Library took advantage of the closure and completed one of the major projects that was
  not done in 10 years – inventory. 25% of the materials that we have didn’t exist or were not
  cataloged correctly. All errors have been identified and fixed.

    Second major change is the Library ILS system. On August 25 th the Mayor and Council
  Members had approved a five year agreement with Sirsi Corporation, to change the
  Library system from Polaris to SirsiDynix Symphony, which is an advanced cloud-based
  solution that will allow the Library to move away from the old hosted server-based system.
  After the initial install the new ILS system is going to move towards bringing on a phone
  app called Blue Cloud Mobile that will allow access to digital library cards and Library
  electronic materials… In addition to all of these benefits that we are getting from the new
  system, it will also bring $22,000 dollars in saving annually.

    We are also working on employee reorganization and already started the cross trainings of
  the staff between 2 libraries to provide better services to patrons.

    We bought $60,000 worth of new furniture specifically for the first floor gap at the Main
  Library and when we go under renovation, everything will be placed at the Crenshaw
  Library.

    DVDs and Magazines were moved from 3rd and 2nd floor to 1st floor. 2nd floor will have
  more space for people to study. Also, computers were moved from 3 rd floor to 2nd floor for
  the patrons to see all the available computers. IT Department will repurpose the computers
  that are not being used and make them available for public use including Children’s
  division and Crenshaw Library. We purchased drop down signage and had them installed
  over various library materials for public to see from far away the items that are available.
  Also, rearrange some furniture, moved some old shelving, emptied 3 rd floor for the
  preparation of the roof repair.

    We bought 15 laptops with hard cases and security software’s for patrons and working on
  laptop lending program. Working with T-Mobile to get 4G pucks that people can take home
  with laptops to have internet access from their home. In addition, we are going to buy
  some Chromebooks with security software for patrons to use in the library.

    Working with company called BMI for some of the important microfiche to get scanned and
  have it on our website, so patrons can have access to all the material online.

    Right now we have curbside pick-up, home delivery and virtual services available for
  patrons.

    We are also partnering with the Senior Center. And all the seniors that are getting food
  delivered, will also get books delivered with food.

    We use a service called Constant Contact to send out monthly newsletters via email to
  5000 emails from our library records about all of our programming including home delivery,
  curbside pick-up and all the rest of virtual services that are available for them.
Board Member Minton asked if a lot of libraries are using the ILS system and number of security officers we
are going to have.

  2
 Deputy to the City Manager Harjinder Singh mentioned some of the libraries that are using the system and
added that we are going to have 2 security officers at the Main Library and 1 security officer at the Branch
Library after opening to the public. But Main Library will have 1 security again when we go back to normal
operations.
Board Member Cochran asked questions about Blue Cloud Mobile app.
Deputy to the City Manager Harjinder Singh explained all the benefits of the mobile app. that will allow
people to have access to digital library cards, reserve and download books to their phone, reserve space
for meetings and some other benefits.
Deputy to the City Manager Harjinder Singh also talked about the budget. Lot of our funding was allocated
incorrectly. After doing some analysis, we have $187,000 dollars of savings in our budget now for
programing, electronics and for the needs of this Library
Board Member Minton asked if Polaris is more or less expensive and if we have money in the budget for
Library Director’s position, if the renovation is still on track and if the library website can be independent
from city page. Minton also had questions about databases and government docs.
Deputy to the City Manager Harjinder Singh told Minton that Polaris is much more expensive and yes we
do have money in the budget for Library Directors position. And city pushed back the renovation by a year.
And when the world goes back to normal they will go back to those plans that were put on hold. Mr.
Harjinder also mentioned that we can redesign but will not be able to have independent page. Per
conversation with Mr. Fields all city departments must have a consistent look and placement.
Principal Librarian over Adult Services Linda Silba answer Board Member Minton’s questions, explained
that we have all the resources online thru our website and spoke about Brainfuse, which is a live tutoring
database for parents and teachers. It also has another site that patrons can log in and get assistance with
resumes and job interview coaching.
Board Member Cochran was very happy with Mr. Singh’s budget explanation and asked to have an annual
budget meeting for them to understand more.
Deputy to the City Manager Harjinder Singh agreed with Board Member Cochran.
Public Comments

  Friends of Inglewood public Library Robin Hunter asked if we are going to keep some of our
databases that can actually be connected to the catalog. And if we are going to buy books and if we are up
to date on best sellers.

  Deputy to the City Manager Singh answered yes, our Principal Librarians are reviewing which
aspects of EBSCO list of items we might want to keep, but there also might be a different way that we get
through it. We are up to date on the best sellers and after finishing the project we’ll complete our offerings
to the public.

Commissioner Comments

  Board Member Douglas liked the fact that we are going to cloud based system and hoping that it
will attract more users to our library remotely.

  3
   Board Member Castillo thanked Mr. Singh for the great report, great work that library is doing. He’s
happy to hear about Library working with T-Mobile to acquire hotspots for students, about laptops and
Chromebooks, about the library being a resource, without having people go into library to choose a
resource. Mr. Castillo emphasize how important is what library’s doing and the great way to move forward.
  All Board members thanked Mr. Singh for the great report and the great job as well.
  Board Member Minton asked if the library is doing any blogs.
  Principal Librarian Linda Silba answered no, we are not doing blogs, but we have a monthly
newsletter which will be on the webpage as we go through the redesign. Principal Librarian Kerri Arroyo
added that we have virtual programming for different age groups. It’s a new territory for librarians, everyone
is doing their best and it’s slowly growing.

  Deputy to the City Manager Harjinder Singh thanked everyone.

  With no further comments the meeting was adjourned at 7:57 p.m.

  4
